knowledge:
- key_parameters: Y=The input data, which can be a SummarizedExperiment, a matrix of counts, or other observed data ;; x=The design matrix (model matrix) ;; log.lik=The log-likelihood function (set to NULL when using fast C++ methods) ;; param=Dispersion parameters (e.g., negative binomial dispersions from DESeq2, or beta-binomial dispersion parameters) ;; coef=The integer index of the coefficient in the design matrix to shrink ;; threshold=A numeric threshold for calculating the probability of a false-sign-or-small (FSOS) event (must be on the natural log scale) ;; mle=A matrix of MLE estimates and their standard errors, scaled to the natural log scale (multiplied by log(2)) ;; offset=A matrix of offsets (e.g., log of size factors) with the same dimensions as the count matrix ;; method=The optimization method to use, such as "nbinomR" (~5x faster), "nbinomCR" (~10x faster, returns posterior SD), "nbinomC" (~50-100x faster, MAP only), "betabinCR" (fast C++ for beta-binomial with SD), or "betabinC" (fast C++ for beta-binomial MAP only) ;; no.shrink=Logical, if TRUE apeglm estimates MLEs without applying shrinkage ;; log.link=Logical, whether to use a log link (set to FALSE for beta-binomial logit link)
- alternatives: DESeq2's "normal" shrinkage type (an older Normal-prior-based method, no longer the default in lfcShrink) ;; zinbwave for zero-inflated negative binomial data (excess zeros down-weighted or modeled via ZINB likelihood)
- when_to_use: Use when you need to shrink GLM coefficients (such as log fold changes in RNA-seq or log-odds ratios in allele-specific expression) to control for high noise in low-count features, and when you want to calculate s-values to control the false sign rate (FSR) or false-sign-or-small (FSOS) rate.
- pitfalls: apeglm estimates coefficients on the natural log scale, whereas DESeq2's lfcShrink interface expects and returns coefficients on the log2 scale. You must multiply log2 values by log(2) before passing them to apeglm, and multiply apeglm outputs by log2(exp(1)) to convert them back to the log2 scale ;; The original general interface (using log.lik=logLikNB) is slow and may cause Lapack errors; always prefer the faster C++ implementations (e.g., method="nbinomCR" or method="betabinCR") ;; P-values and local FSR are on different scales and represent different events (e.g., an FSR of 0.5 is as bad as a random guess).

workflows.name: rna_seq_lfc_shrinkage
workflows.intent: Shrink log fold changes from RNA-seq count data using a negative binomial model to control for low-count noise.
input: airway (SummarizedExperiment containing RNA-seq count data and sample metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter out low-count genes ;; 2. Run DESeq2 to estimate size factors, dispersions, and initial MLE coefficients ;; 3. Extract the design matrix, dispersions, and convert MLEs and offsets to the natural log scale ;; 4. Run apeglm using a fast negative binomial method (e.g., "nbinomR", "nbinomCR", or "nbinomC") ;; 5. Convert the shrunk coefficients back to the log2 scale and compute s-values from the threshold probabilities.
workflows.code:
library(airway)
data(airway)
head(assay(airway))
keep <- head(which(rowSums(assay(airway)) >= 10), 3000)
airway <- airway[keep,]
library(DESeq2)
dds <- DESeqDataSet(airway, ~cell + dex)
dds$dex <- relevel(dds$dex, "untrt")
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds)
x <- model.matrix(design(dds), colData(dds))
param <- dispersions(dds)
mle <- log(2) * cbind(res$log2FoldChange, res$lfcSE)
offset <- matrix(log(sizeFactors(dds)),
                 ncol=ncol(dds),
                 nrow=nrow(dds),byrow=TRUE)
library(apeglm)
system.time({
  fitR <- apeglm(Y=airway, x=x, log.lik=NULL, param=param, coef=ncol(x),
                 threshold=log(2) * 1, mle=mle, offset=offset, method="nbinomR")
})
fit <- fitR
names(fit)
str(fit$prior.control)
system.time({
  fitCR <- apeglm(Y=assay(airway), x=x, log.lik=NULL, param=param, coef=ncol(x),
                 threshold=log(2) * 1, mle=mle, offset=offset, method="nbinomCR")
})
system.time({
  fitC <- apeglm(Y=assay(airway), x=x, log.lik=NULL, param=param, coef=ncol(x),
                 threshold=log(2) * 1, mle=mle, offset=offset, method="nbinomC")
})
class(fit$ranges)
mcols(fit$ranges, use.names=TRUE)
s.val <- svalue(fit$thresh)

workflows.name: beta_binomial_ratio_shrinkage
workflows.intent: Estimate and shrink log-odds ratios for count ratio data (such as allele-specific expression) using a beta-binomial model.
input: ase.cts (matrix of success counts, e.g., allele-specific counts)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize the dispersion estimate ;; 2. Iteratively estimate MLE coefficients using apeglm with no.shrink=TRUE and update the beta-binomial dispersion parameter using bbEstDisp ;; 3. Run apeglm with shrinkage using the estimated dispersion, MLEs, and a threshold ;; 4. Compute s-values from the threshold probabilities to identify significant features.
workflows.code:
library(emdbook)
n <- 20
f <- factor(rep(1:2,each=n))
mu <- ifelse(res$baseMean > 50, res$baseMean, 50)
set.seed(1)
cts <- matrix(rnbinom(nrow(dds)*2*n, 
                      mu=mu,
                      size=1/dispersions(dds)),
              ncol=2*n)
theta <- runif(nrow(cts),1,1000)
prob <- rnorm(nrow(cts),.5,.05) # close to 0.5
ase.cts <- matrix(rbetabinom(prod(dim(cts)), prob=prob,
                             size=cts, theta=rep(theta,ncol(cts))),
                  nrow=nrow(cts))
idx <- 1:10
idx2 <- which(f == 2)
theta[idx] <- 1000
prob[idx] <- 0.75
ase.cts[idx,idx2] <- matrix(rbetabinom(length(idx)*length(idx2), prob=prob[idx],
                                       size=cts[idx,idx2], theta=theta[idx]),
                            nrow=length(idx))
theta.hat <- 100 # rough initial estimate of dispersion
x <- model.matrix(~f)
niter <- 3
system.time({
  for (i in 1:niter) {
    param <- cbind(theta.hat, cts)
    fit.mle <- apeglm(Y=ase.cts, x=x, log.lik=NULL, param=param,
                      no.shrink=TRUE, log.link=FALSE, method="betabinCR")
    theta.hat <- bbEstDisp(success=ase.cts, size=cts,
                           x=x, beta=fit.mle$map,
                           minDisp=.01, maxDisp=5000)
  }
})
mle <- cbind(fit.mle$map[,coef], fit.mle$sd[,coef])
param <- cbind(theta.hat, cts)
system.time({
  fit2 <- apeglm(Y=ase.cts, x=x, log.lik=NULL, param=param,
                 coef=coef, mle=mle, threshold=0.5,
                 log.link=FALSE, method="betabinCR")
})
s.val <- svalue(fit2$thresh)
